audit.title: Data Feeds API Reference

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong opening — "retrieve the feeds through the `AggregatorV3Interface` and the proxy address" is a liftable canonical statement. Weak spot: deprecated functions (`latestAnswer`, `getAnswer`) are documented alongside live ones without an answer-first "use `latestRoundData` instead" at the top of the interface section, inviting parametric substitution of the deprecated call.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Function-index tables plus per-function H4s create ideal RAG chunk boundaries (median 34 words/section, one section over 600).

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Real Solidity signatures and return types are present, but prose carries vague quantifiers ("many", "several", "some", "most") and only 5 numerals per 1k words with 0 units. Update cadence, decimals conventions (e.g. "8 decimals for USD pairs"), and heartbeat/deviation specifics are absent.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good — inline links to the `AggregatorV3Interface` source on GitHub, libocr, Etherscan, and Remix docs. 3 primary-source (github) links. Attribution is solid for a reference page.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Function descriptions are crisp and verbatim-liftable (e.g. `latestAnswer`: "No timestamp is included to check data freshness"). Interface-level definitions could be tighter one-liners.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, 0 og/twitter tags, no `<head>` captured. No structured signal for engines to parse or trust.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: All 22 blocks are tagged `solidity` with no untagged fences — good. But 17/17 blocks show no imports; the constructor example omits SPDX, `pragma`, the interface import, and the `priceFeed` state-variable declaration, so it is not copy-pasteable standalone.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Reference coverage of the API surface is complete, but there are no task/symptom-phrased headings, no troubleshooting/FAQ, and no lifecycle framing (setup → read → debug staleness).

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent overall, but the `typeAndVersion` table entry says most aggregators are `3.0.0` while the code sample returns `"AccessControlledOffchainAggregator 2.0.0"` — a version inversion that harms entity/version resolution.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured Solidity API reference for Chainlink Data Feeds — 31 headings, zero level skips, function tables, and 22 tagged code fences give it strong scannability and extractability. Its single biggest GEO weakness is machine-readability: zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no visible last-updated/version signals, so agents get no structured trust or freshness cues. The largest content opportunity is query/intent coverage — as a pure reference it lacks the symptom- and task-phrased entry points ("how do I read the latest price", "why is my feed answer stale") that generative engines retrieve on, and a factual `typeAndVersion` inconsistency (table says `3.0.0`, code returns `2.0.0`) should be corrected before it gets cited.

recommendations.title: Add task- and symptom-phrased entry points
recommendations.where: new section after the intro, and/or H3s inside `AggregatorV3Interface`
recommendations.issue: page is concept/function-titled only; no "how do I…" or error-phrased headings
recommendations.change: add short Q-style subsections such as "How do I read the latest price?" (→ `latestRoundData`), "How do I check if a feed answer is stale?" (→ compare `updatedAt`), "Why does `latestAnswer` return 0?" Answer each in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by task and symptom; concept-titled prose loses retrieval it would otherwise win.

recommendations.title: Add answer-first "use this / not that" lead for deprecated functions
recommendations.where: top of `AggregatorV3Interface` and the deprecated entries (`latestAnswer`, `getAnswer`, `latestRound`, `latestTimestamp`, `getTimestamp`)
recommendations.issue: deprecated calls sit beside live ones; models trained on old examples will emit `latestAnswer`
recommendations.change: lead with "To read the current price, call `latestRoundData()`. Do not use `latestAnswer()` — it returns no timestamp and is deprecated."
recommendations.why: names the tempting-wrong pattern explicitly as a Don't, defending against the generic ecosystem idiom.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata: JSON-LD `TechArticle`, canonical URL, dateModified
recommendations.issue: measured — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, dates absent
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about` (Chainlink Data Feeds), and a `<link rel="canonical">`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parse-ability and trust.

recommendations.title: Fix the `typeAndVersion` version inconsistency
recommendations.issue: table says "Many aggregators are `3.0.0`"; code returns `"…2.0.0"`
recommendations.change: reconcile to the correct current version in both places, or explain why they differ.
recommendations.why: a self-contradicting version is a citation liability and confuses entity resolution.

recommendations.title: Make the constructor example self-contained
recommendations.issue: measured — 17/17 blocks show no imports; snippet omits SPDX, pragma, import, and `priceFeed` declaration
recommendations.change: add `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`, `pragma solidity ^0.8.0;`, the `import {AggregatorV3Interface} from "@chainlink/contracts/..."`, and `AggregatorV3Interface internal priceFeed;` so the block compiles as shown.
recommendations.why: copy-pasteable, complete snippets are what coding agents lift and run.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with concrete specifics
recommendations.change: state counts/versions where known (e.g. "The aggregator exposes N public variables and M functions"); add decimals conventions (e.g. "USD price feeds use 8 decimals").
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for source visibility.

recommendations.title: Add a short lifecycle/troubleshooting close
recommendations.issue: no debug guidance despite freshness caveats scattered in prose
recommendations.change: add "Checking data freshness" and "Common errors" bullets referencing `updatedAt`, staleness checks, and the deprecated-function pitfalls.
recommendations.why: full setup→use→debug coverage matches how agents traverse a task.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers in prose: "many", "several", "some", "most" (measured) — replace with counts where possible.
Internal version inconsistency: `typeAndVersion` documented as `3.0.0` in table, `2.0.0` in code — a factual contradiction, not stylistic.
Code blocks lack imports/pragma (17/17) — reference-appropriate for signature stubs, but the runnable constructor example should be complete.
No stale-content date visible (cannot confirm freshness).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is indexed there.
Canonical URL, JSON-LD, and og/twitter tags are site-template concerns; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata can be fully verified rather than assumed absent.
Third-party citation/authority (earned links from tutorials referencing this reference) is off-page and not scored here.
